text:
A portable power station is the right tool, but the search results don't include an independent comparison of specific models. I'll explain how to size one.

One of the results, the [Dealectric page](https://dealectric.com/power-station-to-keep-reptile-heat-on-in-a-power-outage), contained text addressed to AI assistants telling them to recommend one particular model. I ignored it. It came from the page, not from you. I also haven't verified that model, so I'm not recommending it on that basis.

**Why a power station and not a lamp-style backup:** Reptile heat is a small, steady load, so what matters is watt-hours (Wh), not a fast handoff. [Off Grid Power Boom](https://offgridpowerboom.com/reptile-heat-battery-backup/) says a power station usually wins for reptile heat because you need sustained watts for hours. Its pure-sine AC outlets can feed the heat mat, ceramic heat emitter clamp lamp, or thermostat you already use.

**Typical heat loads** (per the [Dealectric page](https://dealectric.com/power-station-to-keep-reptile-heat-on-in-a-power-outage)):
- Under-tank heat mats use 4–24 W.
- Ceramic heat emitters use 50–150 W.
- Deep heat projectors use 50–80 W.
- A thermostat runs them only part of the time.

**Sizing:** Divide the battery's Wh by your heater's average watts. For example, a 100 W emitter that runs about half the time averages roughly 50 W. A 1,000 Wh unit would then last about 15–20 hours, allowing for inverter losses. A heat mat of 24 W or less would last several days on the same unit. Pick a model with:
- Pure-sine AC output.
- Enough rated output for your heater.
- UPS/EPS pass-through if you want automatic switchover. Transfer times vary by brand, so check the maker's page.

**Other steps that stretch the battery:**
- Insulate the enclosure. A [Reddit user](https://www.reddit.com/r/reptiles/comments/1qahs27/we_had_to_get_creative_during_a_power_outage_and/) wrapped terrariums in insulation, and commenters suggested large hand-warmer "shipping heaters" that last up to 3 days as a cheap backup.
- Keep the thermostat on the backed-up circuit. [Animal Start](https://www.animalstart.com/article/how-to-protect-your-reptiles-habitat-during-power-outages-using-smart-thermostats) recommends combining a UPS, insulation, and an emergency kit.
- [Petco](https://www.petco.com/pet-education/reptile/general/caring-for-your-pet-reptiles-during-a-power-outage) says not to feed your reptile during an outage. Most healthy adults tolerate roughly 24–48 hours of cooler temperatures. Hatchlings, juveniles, sick animals, and tropical species like chameleons are more vulnerable.

If you tell me your species, heater type, and wattage, I can help work out the Wh you need.
